Priya: Quick flag - brought up rk-small-quant (post-PTQ) on holdout and seeing NDCG up but MRR down, feels like top1 churn.
Priya: Summary: NDCG@10 +0.015, MRR@10 -0.031. Run ids: baseline run://2026-03-10/rk-small-fp16 (sha: d4f1e2), quant run://2026-03-24/rk-small-ptq (sha: e7c2b9).
Omar: Sounds like tie instability. Did you compare per-query top1 equality?
Priya: Ran a quick compare: top1_changed = 4.8% of queries on the holdout. Most flips are where score diffs < 0.002.
Tess: For that delta range, tokenization or tiny normalizer differences can push lexical tiebreakers. Any serializer diffs between eval vs prod candidate dumps?
Priya: I checked serial hashes, we do have two serializers active in the pipeline (legacy_html and compact). The eval harness used compact; prod still uses legacy_html for a subset of customers.
Omar: That will do it. Suggest two mitigations: 1) introduce deterministic tiebreaker policy in eval that mirrors prod (stable doc_id fallback) 2) add a soft-tie smoothing in scoring: score = softmax_temper_adjust(score, eps=1e-3) so micro-noise doesn't reorder top1 often.
Tess: Also run a lexical-stability probe: rerank.eval --runs baseline,quant --per-query --tiebreak=lexical,stable. Count flips where lexical vs score disagree.
Priya: Doing the lexical probe now. Quick result on 10k sample: lexical-stable reduces top1 flips to 1.1%, MRR delta improves from -0.031 to -0.008 (on sample).
Omar: Good signal. If lexical-stable helps, we can gate quant models to enable stable tiebreaker by default, or better, make tiebreaker configurable per model variant.
Tess: We should also add a normalization parity check in onboarding: compare candidate tokenization and a normalized sha for both serializers. Small script: 
```
# parity check
python -m rerank.tools.serializer_parity \
  --a s3://eval/candidates.json \
  --b s3://prod/candidates.json \
  --out parity_report.json
```
Priya: Ran that: 2.2% candidates differ, mostly HTML-entity vs unescaped and non-breaking-space chars. I'll open a ticket to unify serializers.
Omar: For the quant side, try a tiny calibration tweak: rerank-quant --calib-bins 256 vs 512 and see if distribution compression changes tie frequency.
Priya: Will run anchor of calib bins and also test a small smoothing layer: when abs(score_a - score_b) < 1e-3, prefer lexical order. Running these tests now.
eval-bot: job run://2026-03-24/rk-small-ptq completed. metrics: NDCG@10: 0.678 -> 0.693, MRR@10: 0.401 -> 0.370.
Tess: Please record cohort breakdown by query length and candidate-dup presence. Short queries and de-duplicated pools usually show most flips.
Priya: Noted. I'll post final full-holdout numbers after parity PR. Also adding a small CI gate: on onboarding, ensure top1_flip_rate < 2% vs baseline on a 10k sample or require review.
Omar: 👍 good plan. Make the tiebreaker toggle behind feature-flag so we can iterate on fielded traffic easily.
Priya: Will do, filing PRs for serializer parity + tiebreaker toggle + quant calibration notebook.
